receipt.public_excerpt: Concerns over a persistent cost-of-living crisis and the intertwined risks of AI-driven misinformation and disinformation, and societal polarization dominated the risks outlook for 2024.

evidence_items.explanation: A major mainstream body said AI-driven misinformation dominated its 2024 risk outlook, three months before the post. That shows the concern had reached the mainstream.

receipt.public_excerpt: Misinformation and disinformation are biggest short-term risks

evidence_items.explanation: More than 1,400 surveyed experts ranked misinformation first among short-term global risks, a sign of very broad institutional concern.

receipt.public_excerpt: Most adults (58%) believe that the use of AI will increase the spread of misinformation during the 2024 presidential election

evidence_items.explanation: A representative US poll found most adults expected AI to increase election misinformation. Concern was widespread among the public, not just experts.

receipt.public_excerpt: Overall, 54% of adults have not read or heard much at all about AI

evidence_items.explanation: A caveat: many adults still knew little about AI itself, so public awareness was uneven.

unresolved_gaps: No cited source directly compares awareness in early 2024 with an earlier baseline, so the 'more broadly' trend is inferred from high levels rather than measured as a change.
